tweets.text: SPLASHDOWN IN TEXAS! On 5/27, smugglers tried to outsmart the U.S. Border Patrol with a bold move—floating a pickup truck loaded with suspicious bundles across the Rio Grande on a homemade raft. Once on U.S. soil, they made a break for it. But as agents closed in, the driver veered back and plunged the truck into the river in a desperate attempt to escape. Chaos followed as individuals scrambled in the water to retrieve the suspected narcotics—but USBP agents acted fast. They recovered 6 bundles of marijuana weighing nearly 250 lbs. Smugglers are getting bolder, but USBP always stands at the ready.

tweets.text:
Laredo, TX – Two juveniles were arrested by U.S. Border Patrol agents after they were caught guiding eight illegal aliens across the Rio Grande into the United States. Agents identified the teens as brush guides, responsible for smuggling individuals through dangerous terrain to avoid detection. Despite their age, both now face criminal prosecution for alien smuggling.

The consequences are real — regardless of age. Criminal organizations continue to exploit youth, but law enforcement remains vigilant.

tweets.text:
Yuma, AZ – On May 28, Border Patrol agents apprehended a documented Paisas gang member attempting to re-enter the United States illegally — for the 11th time. The Mexican national has a lengthy history of immigration violations and criminal activity. He admitted to joining the Paisas gang 25 years ago, during a previous incarceration stemming from an immigration-related offense.

Now, he faces felony prosecution for illegal re-entry under 8 USC §1326. Repeat offenders will face consequences. Gang ties and prior arrests reinforce the need for swift legal action.

tweets.text:
METH SEIZURE ON A FLORIDA HIGHWAY!

On May 21, USBP agents and the Marion County Narcotics Task Force stopped a smuggler’s vehicle in its tracks during a coordinated operation. A K9 alerted to a hidden compartment — inside, agents discovered 181 pounds of meth. Authorities also seized $10,000 in cash as evidence. Two U.S. citizens are now in custody and face prosecution under 21USC844 for possession of a controlled substance.

Sharp eyes. Strong teamwork. Serious results.
